cells.tense: You are holding what matters and staying reachable, right here, with both hands on it.
cells.ask: Tell one person the real version this week, not the tidy one, and let it land how it lands.
cells.core:
You can bear weight and remain someone people can still get to. What you hold doesn't make you rigid and it doesn't make you drop it. You keep your shape under pressure and you're still in the room with whoever's there.

The teaching, the shared thing you care about — it moves through you and it lands, because you're present in it rather than braced against it. What this steadiness can feed next is naming what you actually bear, plainly, without hardening it or dressing it up. You already hold form under pressure. Let one other person see the shape of it, said straight.
cells.sheetLine: You carry it and stay reachable. That's the whole thing.
cells.verb: carrying feeling into shared meaning, teaching what connects
cells.place: where you bear weight and keep your form under it

cells.tense: You are bracing for a future where they finally understand, and pushing toward it before anyone asked.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're pushing and leave it alone for a day. Say it once, no follow-up.
cells.core:
You're bearing more than has arrived. Ahead of you is a version where the meaning lands and the people around you get it, and you're living in that version already — so a conversation turns into a chance to move them there. The effort that was for holding steady is going into steering.

What you're pushing toward is real. Meaning does travel between people. But it travels at its own pace, and you're trying to carry it for the whole room. Your ability to hold isn't gone. It's braced against something not here yet. Put one thing down and leave it down for the day. What needs to shift will still be there tomorrow, and you'll be standing.

cells.tense: You stopped handing over what you know a while back, and part of you still stands at that door.
cells.ask: Tell one person one thing you understand, unfinished, before the week is out.
cells.core:
The connection is there and the handing over isn't. What you know about meaning, about what draws people together, stays inside you — and bearing it alone is heavier than bearing it out loud, because nothing shared is taking any of the weight. You hold the shape and keep the people near you at a distance from it.

What's absent isn't stamina, and it isn't something worth saying. It's the delivery. Don't force feeling into the place that's running dry. Work on the thinking instead — get clear on what you actually understand well enough to give away, and say it once. The door is behind you. The telling doesn't need to be good. It needs to happen.
cells.sheetLine: You have the form and you've stopped handing it over.

cells.tense: You are already shaping what people around you find meaningful, and you'd say it's just how things go.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, that this thing you call 'how it goes' is something you meant.
cells.core:
You hold your form under pressure and you do it in company — the words you reach for, what you bring up again, what you let land and what you let pass by. That's already teaching. It's already setting what connects for the people near you. But you describe it like the room is doing it, or the work is, or the way things are.

The bearing is real and so is the making. You've been letting the shared meaning keep your name off it. Claim the one thing you'd call just how things go, and let it be yours. That's not a claim on anyone else. It's the earlier, simpler form of the same thing: you meant it, you made it, it's yours.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person's endurance is currently holding the emotional intensity of teaching or ritual — the record gives the card and seat but not their life, so every cell stays with the mechanism instead of their story. A reader could reasonably say the seat is Fortitude in the Seed stage, not a person currently bearing weight, so no cell says what they are carrying or who put it there. The ask survives being wrong because each one is doable even if the diagnosis is off — telling one person badly, writing down what kept, sitting on one feeling for a day, or saying 'this is mine' all teach something on their own. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is the one that would name a specific past room where saying it didn't go well; that stays out, and Too Little locates the person behind the present without saying what happened there.
